notes:
Top-line: enterprise procurement focused on Dedicated + Private bundle. Heavy SLA negotiation. High sensitivity to uptime credits and maintenance windows. Short timeline (legal target Apr 2026).

Recent timeline (bullets):
- 2025-11-02: Intro / discovery (AE Sofia). Identified use cases: high-volume chat for claims intake + reranking for doc search.
- 2026-01-18: Tech deep-dive with SE (Marcus). Discussed reserved GPU topology (pref H100-class), KV cache behavior, and workload distribution across regions.
- 2026-02-15: Initial commercial proposal delivered (dedicated pool: 4x H100-equivalent nodes, burst to 8), draft ARR shown ~$700k/yr.
- 2026-03-04: SLA redline meeting with Legal + Security. Customer submitted counter-proposal on uptime and credit schedule. (fireflies FF-1633)
- 2026-03-10: Follow-up call re: maintenance windows and KMS audit timeline.

Customer technical / SLA requirements (summary):
- Uptime target: negotiating 99.995% preferred, legal initially willing to accept 99.99% with stronger credits.
- Credit schedule proposed by customer: if monthly uptime <99.995 then 10% service credit; <99.99 then 25%; <99.9 then 50%. They pushed for automatic credits; our legal asks for claim process.
- Support response SLAs: P1 initial response <= 15 minutes, P1 on-call escalation to onshore engineer within 1 hour; P2 <= 1 hour; P3 <= 4 hours. 24/7 coverage required for P1.
- Maintenance windows: customer requests max 6 planned windows/year, each <=30 minutes, 72h scheduled notice; no planned maintenance during end-of-month close windows (1st-3rd of month).
- Throughput guarantees: baseline sustained throughput for production workload ~120k tokens/sec aggregate across dedicated pool; tail p99 generation latency target <120ms for 256-token requests.
- Reserved GPU planning: baseline 4xH100-equivalent nodes (pinned), burst to 8 for peak; requirement to guarantee reserved CPU/GPU allocation and hot standby capacity for failover.
- Routing/fallback: policy to route to quantized fallback model when capacity constrained but maintain p95 latency within SLO; explicit permission to use model variants for failover.
- Security/compliance: SSO/SAML, audit logs retention 3 years, KMS integration (customer-managed), and ISO27001 attestation required. Data residency: US only for PII workloads.

Sales / commercial notes and positions:
- Customer willing to pay premium for tighter uptime but legal pushing back on large automatic credits. Finance wants cap on total credits per quarter.
- Procurement expects final MSA + SLA signed by Apr 2026.
- Est ARR range revised after feature asks: $500k-$1.5M (depends on reserved counts + support add-on).

Quotes / call snippets: 
- "We need predictable latency during our peak claims window — downtime is measured in lost revenue and regulatory risk." — Head of Platform
- "Support must be 24/7 and reachable; CFO will not accept open-ended credits without cap." — Procurement lead

POC / technical milestones:
- We completed a 2-week performance POC in Jan; validated throughput on representative payloads (results in drive sheet).
- Next POC ask: full failover test (canary to fallback model) and KMS key rotation test (scheduled by 2026-03-25).

Next steps (short):
- Legal: push our standard credit claim flow + propose compromise credit cap (SE to draft redline language).
- Commercial: agree final reserved GPU count and finalize price table (Marcus + Sofia).
- Security: schedule KMS audit window and send attestation docs (Elena coordinating).

Open blockers (short):
- Legal redline on uptime/automatic credits (primary).
- Timing for third-party KMS audit (customer insists on independent report).
- Exact reserved unit count — internal cost sensitivity vs their throughput ask.
public_notes_summary: Enterprise insurer evaluating Redwood Dedicated + Private. Negotiating 99.995% vs 99.99% uptime, strong support SLAs (P1 15m), credit schedule and maintenance window constraints. Reserved GPU count pending. Legal redline is primary blocker.
